outline_section.learning_goal: Define delay as a right shift and establish the mapping rule for features and support intervals.

image_policy.image_description_seed: Two-panel signal graph showing $x(t)$ and $y(t)=x(t-T)$, where every feature and interval is moved right by $T$.
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Keep a clean Cartesian grid, same axis scale in both panels, and one clearly visible shift arrow from $t_0$ to $t_0+T$.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Teach the exact delay operator: $y(t)=x(t-T)$, and that this moves each point to the right by $T$ while preserving amplitude and shape.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Single peak at the origin moved to $t = T$.
paragraph_plan: Introduce delay as rightward translation in the time domain.
State the algebraic rule $y(t)=x(t-T)$ and explain meaning term-by-term.
Map a tagged point: $t_0 \mapsto t_0+T$ with unchanged value.
Map support: interval $[a,b] \mapsto [a+T,b+T]$ and preserve piecewise pattern.
Preview why examples then add controlled wrinkles: one point, multiple points, interval boundaries, finite support with breakpoints.

solution_step_plan: Not applicable for tutorial section.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Keep this section short and tightly scaffolded; no questions. Use the graph image as the single conceptual anchor before moving to examples.

prompt_blocks.text: The graph shows one peak at $t=1$ in $x(t)$. If $y(t)=x(t-4)$, where is that peak in $y(t)$?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: A delay by $T$ moves the feature time from $t_0$ to $t_0+T$. Here $t_0=1$ and $T=4$, so the peak moves to $1+4=5$.

outline_section.learning_goal: Shift multiple marked feature points consistently and maintain their relative order and values.

image_policy.image_description_seed: Piecewise graph with several key points and a delayed version shifted right by $T$, with all point labels visible.
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Reuse the same basic shape and change the key-point coordinates or $T$ in mirror questions.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Given a graph with points at $t=-1$, $0$, and $2$ delayed by $T = 4$, ask which option lists all delayed point times correctly.
distractor_plan: Apply left-shift instead of right-shift on one or more points.
Drop one key point or duplicate a shifted point.
Shift by the wrong sign or magnitude while keeping spacing.
Alter point heights while shifting times correctly.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Take a signal with key points $(-2,3)$, $(0,-1)$, and $(3,2)$. Delay by $T = 2$. List all delayed key-point times with values.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: The learner applies $t \mapsto t+T$ to each point while preserving values: $(-2,3) \to (0,3)$, $(0,-1) \to (2,-1)$, $(3,2) \to (5,2)$.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Moves from one-point timing shift to coordinated multi-point mapping without changing interval handling yet.
solution_step_plan: Write $y(t)=x(t-T)$.
Mark each original key point time and value.
Add $T$ to each time coordinate.
Keep each value unchanged and preserve shape order.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Emphasize uniform time mapping across all points; avoid changing signs or amplitudes in options.

prompt_blocks.text: The plot shows $x(t)$ and the fixed delay $T=4$. Which choice lists the delayed key points of $y(t)=x(t-4)$ as time-value pairs?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Delay means add the same $T$ to every time coordinate and keep each value unchanged.
The other choices either shift left, use the wrong amount of shift, duplicate or drop a point, or change the heights.

question_policy.practice_question_model: If $x(t)$ is nonzero on $[-1,4]$, delayed by $T = 3$, ask for the support interval of $y(t)$.
distractor_plan: Use $[-1-T,4-T]$ to model sign confusion.
Use $[-1,4]$ to model no-delay confusion.
Shift only one endpoint.
Swap endpoint order or confuse open and closed interval notation.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Given that $x(t)$ is nonzero on $2 \le t \le 6$, delay by $T = 1.5$ and specify the support of $y(t)$.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: The learner shifts both endpoints by $+T$ to conclude $3.5 \le t \le 7.5$ with no change in nonzero magnitude pattern.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Extends point mapping to interval-level mapping while keeping arithmetic structure simple.
solution_step_plan: Write support of $x(t)$ as $[a,b]$.
Apply the delay rule to produce $y(t)=x(t-T)$.
Shift interval endpoints: $[a+T, b+T]$.
State zero outside the shifted interval.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Keep support notation explicit; practice should include both inclusive and exclusive interval forms where helpful.

prompt_blocks.text: If $x(t)$ is nonzero on $[-2,3]$ and $y(t)=x(t-4)$, what is the support interval of $y(t)$?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: A delay adds the same $T$ to both endpoints. Here, $-2+4=2$ and $3+4=7$.
